bat-removal.intro: Folly Beach's bat work lives in its older beach houses — the raised cottages and pre-war homes behind Center Street whose rooflines have been re-shingled, re-flashed, and patched against the salt air for decades. Brazilian free-tailed bats take the fascia gaps and roof voids of that stock, feeding at dusk over the Folly River marshes and the island's west end, and a colony can occupy a quiet rental attic for a full season before a guest or a cleaner notices the smell. Storm-tired trim is the island's chronic entry point: every hurricane season works the fascia a little looser, and the free-tails find the loosening first.
bat-removal.extendedBody:
Free-tails in the Folly roofline

Exclusion on Folly is a materials job as much as an animal job. Salt air corrodes standard screen and fasteners within a few seasons, so we map every entry — free-tailed colonies use several small gaps rather than one obvious hole — and seal in marine-tolerant metal and mesh, timed to SCDNR's guidance: South Carolina fixes no statutory bat dates, but sealing while pups are flightless traps them inside, and we will not do it; a colony found in early summer is mapped in full and excluded when the young are flying. Rental properties get the complete record in photographs, because an owner in another state cannot walk a Folly roofline, and the property manager needs the entry-by-entry account. No permit is required for bat exclusion here — but a bat inside the living space is different: close the room, keep guests and pets clear, and call the same day, and if there was any contact, SC DPH reporting is part of the handling.

faqs.q: Our Folly Beach rental has bats in the attic and guests arriving. What happens first?
faqs.a: The inspection and the guest question are separated. Guests are not at risk from a sealed attic colony overhead — bats do not enter living spaces unless a gap connects them, and checking for that gap is part of the first visit. The exclusion itself is scheduled to the bats' calendar, not the rental calendar: if pups are flightless, the colony is mapped and staged and the exclusion happens the moment the window is right, usually between rental turns. What we will not do is seal a maternity colony in for a checkout deadline — it fails, it is inhumane, and it leaves dead bats in the roof. You get a written plan with dates your manager can book around.

faqs.q: How much does bat removal cost on Folly Beach?
faqs.a: It depends on the colony size and how many entries the roofline carries — older Folly homes with decades of patched fascia are at the larger end. We inspect, map every gap, and quote the complete exclusion with salt-air-rated sealing materials before any work starts. The quote includes the photographic record for owners and managers, and if the colony must wait for the pups to fly, the mapping is done now and the exclusion is held at the quoted price for its scheduled window.
